blocks.text: Fist hit Jaws before he reached the tank.
blocks.alt: Fist punches Jaws into the stone wall above the arrest scene as Laura remains with her police escort.

blocks.text: The red glove came out of nowhere. Jaws shot sideways above the police car and struck the stone wall with a crack. Dust puffed around his hair.
The officer with the extinguisher ducked. His partner kept Laura beside the open door.
Fist stopped in front of the fresh mark on the wall.
“That’s for what you did to me!”
Jaws shook the dust out of his hair. His iron teeth scraped together.
“I don’t know who you are, but I know I don’t like you.”
Fist’s eyes narrowed.
Didn’t know him?
Jaws looked him over, from his red knuckles to his white cuff.
“If you’re still flying, I must have let you off easy. Not this time, glove!”
blocks.alt: Jaws bares his iron teeth at Fist beside the fresh mark in the wall, with no recognition in his eyes.

blocks.text: His jaws opened wide.
Fist jerked upward.
The teeth clanged shut just behind his cuff.
blocks.alt: Fist darts upward as Jaws snaps his iron teeth shut on empty air behind the glove’s white cuff.

blocks.text: He swung back and clipped the side of the iron jaw. Jaws spun away from the car, caught himself and charged again.
Fist climbed past the windows. Jaws followed.
Jenny watched them clear the street, then turned toward the sound of tracks scraping pavement.
The tank was moving.
Across the square, Billy waved two people into the side street. An officer took over at the corner. Seth waited until they were past him before stepping out from behind a stone planter.
Above them, Fist swerved around a projecting ledge.
Jaws cut across the turn. Metal teeth flashed where Fist’s cuff had been.
Fist dropped, came up beneath him and landed a quick punch against the jaw.
Jaws rocked backward.
Then he grinned.
“Hold still!”
Fist shot over the roofline.
He remembered those teeth. The torn cuff. The long wait before he could fly out with his friends again.
But Jaws had looked at him as though none of it had happened.
Fist couldn’t make sense of that. There was no recognition in those eyes. Only the mean streak seemed to be left.
A snap behind him ended the thought.
He banked between two rooftops. Far below, a bus stood at an empty stop. Beyond the buildings, Terminal Tower rose into the blue sky.
blocks.alt: Fist and bodyless Jaws chase above Cleveland’s stone rooftops with Terminal Tower beyond.

blocks.text: Jaws came after him, teeth open.
Fist dipped around the corner of a stone parapet.
Jaws rushed past.
The glove turned.
This time his knuckles caught the iron jaw squarely from the side. Jaws tumbled over the empty roof, blond hair whipping around his face.
blocks.alt: Fist turns at a rooftop corner and punches Jaws’s iron jaw over the empty roof.

blocks.text: Fist held his place.
Jaws stopped tumbling. His eyes found the glove again.
He came back faster.
Fist darted away, and their chase carried on above the next street.
Below, Seth stepped into the tank’s path.
Dork spotted the blue suit and red cape. The tracks stopped with a squeal.
“Too late!” he shouted from the driver’s opening.
Jenny came around the planter on the other side, keeping low.
Billy pointed from the corner.
“The ray’s in the turret! Stay out of its line!”
Seth looked up at the short copper rings. They pointed past him toward Terminal Tower.
Dork leaned over his firing control.
“Let’s see Cleveland bow without that!”
Seth rushed the tank.
Jenny slipped clear of its forward line. Seth planted his boots beside the front armor and drove his fist into the side of the turret.
Metal shrieked. The mounting buckled, wrenching the copper opening away from the tower just as Dork pressed the control.
A blue ray flashed across the sky.
blocks.alt: Zerdo punches the side of the attached turret as Dork fires, sending a blue ray away from intact Terminal Tower into the distance.

blocks.text: It missed Terminal Tower and streaked away into the distance.
Dork stared after it.
The tower still stood above the square, every window where it belonged.
Seth kept one hand against the hull. The turret sat crooked on its mounting, but the ray was still inside it.
High above the roofs, iron teeth clanged shut on empty air again.
Seth reached for the turret.
